subject.title: Feature: Session labels / nicknames for easier identification

question: Should OpenClaw standardize user-editable session names on the existing `label`/`/name` contract, migrate to a canonical `title` contract, or expose `/label` and `openclaw sessions label` only as aliases over one of those fields?
rationale: Current main and open PRs implement overlapping but different naming surfaces, and choosing the durable field/command contract affects stored session metadata, CLI/API docs, and upgrade compatibility.

options.title: Keep the existing label contract
options.body: Use `label` as the durable field, keep `/name` as the primary chat command, and implement `/label` or CLI `sessions label` only as aliases that call the same Gateway patch path.

options.title: Migrate to canonical title
options.body: Adopt the open title-contract direction, with explicit compatibility behavior for existing label consumers before adding CLI and chat aliases.

options.title: Narrow to Control UI only
options.body: Land only the Control UI `/new <name>` and `/label` work and leave the broader CLI command/listing request open or explicitly out of scope.

recommendation.title: Keep the existing label contract
recommendation.body: Use `label` as the durable field, keep `/name` as the primary chat command, and implement `/label` or CLI `sessions label` only as aliases that call the same Gateway patch path.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a product/API contract decision spanning CLI, Gateway protocol, Control UI, and persisted session metadata, and this handle is the best available owner signal from CODEOWNERS plus recent central session-surface history.
